summary: Provides guidelines for administering and running public Network Information Center databases with privacy and accuracy in mind. It is informational.

eli5.summary: Rules for being careful with a public phone book of the Internet, so the facts are right and people's private details are protected.

questions: how should network directories protect personal information
subtitle: Guidelines for public network directories to protect privacy and ensure accuracy

tldr.problem: Network Information Centers maintain publicly accessible databases with personal and organizational information, but these often lack clear policies about who can access what data and whether entries are kept accurate.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC recommends that each NIC establish explicit privacy and accuracy policies covering what data is collected, who gets access, how people can correct errors, and what happens if they refuse to provide information.
tldr.outcome: Clear guidelines help NICs handle personal data responsibly while maintaining the utility of public directories for network administration.

today: RFC 1355 is an Informational RFC from August 1992. It provides foundational guidance for operating public network directories responsibly, setting expectations for privacy disclosure and accuracy that remain relevant to any public registry of personal or organizational information.

sections.title: Privacy and Accuracy in Public Network Directories
sections.content:
RFC 1355 provides guidelines for administering Network Information Center (NIC) databases that are publicly accessible. A NIC collects and distributes information about networks, people, organizations, and resources. The RFC addresses the tension between making directory information available for efficient network administration and protecting the privacy and accuracy of personal and organizational data.

The document is organized into two parts: privacy considerations for preventing unauthorized disclosure, and accuracy guidelines for maintaining data quality.
sections.eli5: A NIC is like the Internet's phone book. This standard explains how to balance making information available to those who need it with protecting people's privacy.

sections.title: Privacy Policy Requirements
sections.content:
For each publicly accessible database, a NIC must provide a clear privacy policy that explains to people listed in the database what information the NIC collects and how it will be used. The policy should detail:

  • Why the NIC needs the information and what it will do with it
  • The complete list of information being stored in each entry
  • Which information will be shared outside the NIC, to whom, and for what purpose
  • How people are notified if they are added to the database at someone else's request
  • How to change or update information
  • How to get information removed, including references in other people's entries
  • What consequences follow from refusing to provide information

The policy empowers individuals to make informed decisions about what information to supply.
sections.eli5: Before you let anyone use a list of people, tell them what you will do with their information, who will see it, and how they can change or remove their entry.

sections.title: Accuracy and Data Quality Procedures
sections.content:
Each NIC should maintain an accuracy statement documenting the procedures it uses to keep database entries correct and current. The statement should allow individuals to access their own entries (including private fields) to correct errors, and enable them to correct mistakes that do occur.

Key practices include notifying people when information about them appears in another's entry so they can submit corrections, changing entries only at the request of the person the entry describes, encouraging people to report errors in others' entries, maintaining a 'date of last review' for each entry, and documenting the data validation practices and backup procedures the NIC uses.
sections.eli5: Keep the information in your directory current by letting people fix mistakes about themselves and telling them when someone else mentions their name.

sections.title: Security Aspects
sections.content: The RFC briefly considers security aspects of information in NIC databases. It notes that as security infrastructure in the Internet becomes more developed, the recommendations in this memo may need to be revisited to account for stronger protections.
sections.eli5: With better security tools, there might be better ways to protect personal information in the future.

references.text: North American Directory Forum's "User Bill of Rights for Entries and Listings in the Public Directory", RFC 1295.
